NJ-2026-A5739.title: Authorizes temporary waiver of ABC winery license fees.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Oversight, Reform and Federal Relations Committee

NJ-2026-A5739.aiSummary: The bill would temporarily waive fees charged by the state alcohol office for plenary winery, farm winery, and out-of-State winery licenses. It would apply to people or businesses applying for or holding those licenses, and it would cover license, filing, renewal, transfer, salesroom, and other related fees. The waiver would last for the first two full state fiscal years after the bill becomes law and would not end state or federal taxes or municipal fees.

NJ-2026-A5734.title: Requires State agencies to file notice of intent for proposed rules with certain economic impacts.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Oversight, Reform and Federal Relations Committee

NJ-2026-A5734.aiSummary: State agencies would have to file a notice of intent before starting the formal rulemaking process for a major rule. A major rule is one that could cost more than $10 million a year or at first, or one that could significantly affect local government operations. The rule would apply to State agencies in New Jersey and would take effect 30 days after it is enacted.

NJ-2026-A5725.title: Lifts ban on State and local law enforcement cooperation with federal civil immigration authorities and creates fund to support cooperation; makes an appropriation; repeals section 3 of P.L.2026, c.5.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Public Safety and Preparedness Committee

NJ-2026-A5725.aiSummary: The bill would repeal a 2026 state rule that limits state and local police cooperation with federal civil immigration authorities. It would create a grant program in the Department of Law and Public Safety to help police agencies enter into, renew, or expand certain federal immigration agreements, and it would require a yearly report on the program. The Legislature would be allowed to provide money for the program, and the bill would take effect right away.

NJ-2026-A5720.title: Requires additional monitoring and enforcement of certain orders of compliance and corrective action plans issued during special education disputes.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Education Committee

NJ-2026-A5720.aiSummary: The bill would require the Education Commissioner to oversee follow-up on certain orders and correction plans issued after special education complaints. It would affect school districts and other public or private education agencies that serve students with disabilities, and it would also require reports to the commissioner and the person who filed the complaint. If a school or agency still does not comply, the commissioner would have to give notice and could use enforcement steps such as extra monitoring, training, fund limits, payment holds, or referral to the Attorney General.

NJ-2026-A5716.title: Requires DOT to study and report on pedestrian safety on South Lakeshore Drive in Township of Pemberton.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Transportation and Independent Authorities Committee

NJ-2026-A5716.aiSummary: The Department of Transportation would study pedestrian safety on South Lakeshore Drive in Pemberton Township and work with the township on the study. It would look at speeding, crashes, and pedestrian injuries and deaths, and then send a report with its findings and ideas to reduce those harms. The act would take effect right away and end after the report is sent.

NJ-2026-A5441.title: Revises certain deadlines and State funding regarding support provided by DHS, DOLWD, and Office of Volunteerism to NJ FamilyCare and SNAP recipients to meet federal eligibility requirements via volunteering.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (78-0-0)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee

NJ-2026-A5441.aiSummary: The bill would change the timeline for state help that lets NJ FamilyCare and SNAP applicants and recipients report volunteer or community service hours to meet federal rules. It would require the Department of Human Services and the Department of Labor and Workforce Development to share data and track work and volunteer hours, and it affects people using those programs. It would also shift $50,000 to Human Services and $50,000 to Labor from an existing appropriation for the Office of Volunteerism.

NJ-2026-A5040.title: Establishes Hope Card Program to provide victims of domestic violence with restraining order quick reference wallet card; makes appropriation.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (79-0-0)
Reported out of Assembly Comm. with Amendments, 2nd Reading
Transferred to Assembly Community Development and Women's Affairs Committee
Reported out of Asm. Comm. with Amendments, and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Public Safety and Preparedness Committee

NJ-2026-A5040.aiSummary: The bill would create a Hope Card program for people protected by a final domestic violence restraining order. It would give them a free wallet-size card or secure electronic record with key order details, and it would let courts, police, judges, and court staff use the program with new training. It would also make a yearly state appropriation from the General Fund for the Judiciary and take effect on the first day of the 13th month after it becomes law.

NJ-2026-A3407.title: Prohibits institutions of higher education from requiring students who have children to purchase meal plans, live in on-campus housing, or pay gym fees.

actions.text: Assembly Floor Amendment Passed (Quijano) (Voice)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Higher Education Committee

NJ-2026-A3407.aiSummary: The bill would bar colleges and other higher education schools from making students who have children buy meal plans, live in campus housing, or pay gym fees. It would affect students with children at those schools. The Secretary of Higher Education would have to issue rules within six months after the bill becomes law to help schools check who qualifies for the exemption.

NJ-2026-A2007.title: Requires certain providers to perform intimate partner violence screenings and all health care professionals to take certain actions to prevent perpetrators of intimate partner violence from obtaining copies of victim's medical record.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (79-0-0)
Assembly Floor Amendment Passed (Quijano) (Voice)
Reported out of Assembly Comm. with Amendments, 2nd Reading
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Community Development and Women's Affairs Committee

NJ-2026-A2007.aiSummary: The bill would require some health care providers to screen for intimate partner violence and would require health care workers to take steps to keep a victim’s medical record from reaching the person who hurt them. It would also let a patient who may be a victim get referrals to other health care professionals when needed. The state would make a list of services and resources for victims available around New Jersey.
